blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Her husband had been one of the prophets, a man who feared the LORD. Now he was gone, and he left a debt she could not pay. And the creditor was coming to take her two boys to work it off.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She did not sit quiet with her trouble, Church. She cried out to the prophet Elisha.

verses.text: And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.

segments.speaker: elisha
segments.text: What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She told him she had nothing in the house but one pot of oil. That is all. One pot, two boys, and a debt she could not pay.

verses.text: Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.

segments.speaker: elisha
segments.text: Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.

verses.text: And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.

segments.speaker: elisha
segments.text: And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That was a strange word. Borrow empty jars from all your neighbors. Not a few. Then go inside, shut the door, and start pouring.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Think about what that meant. She had to go door to door and ask. Her neighbors would see her need. Then she had to trust God behind a closed door, with only her sons watching.

verses.text: So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, borrow not a few. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Borrow not a few"] Borrow not a few. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Borrow not a few"] The oil kept coming as long as she had a jar to hold it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The oil kept flowing as long as there was an empty jar. When the last jar was full, it stopped.

verses.text: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She went and told Elisha, the man of God. He told her to sell the oil, pay the debt, and live on the rest with her sons. Her boys were free. That household was saved.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Now hear me. This is a story about God caring for a widow and her children in a desperate hour. It is not a promise that giving or pouring will make anybody rich. Elisha did not ask her for a dime, and she did not pay for a miracle. She brought her need to God's prophet, did what she was told, and God gave her enough to keep her family together.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: And notice the neighbors. Their empty jars became part of the miracle. Sometimes God's help comes through a community willing to lend what they have.
